what: The Hartford is an American insurer. It sells property and casualty insurance to businesses, especially small and mid-sized ones, personal car and home insurance through the AARP partnership, and group disability and life insurance to employers.
customers: Small and mid-sized businesses, employers buying group benefits, and older American consumers through AARP.
money: commercial property, liability and workers' compensation
car and home insurance, largely through AARP
moat: A century of workers' compensation claims data that lets it price small business risk more accurately than newer entrants, plus the exclusive AARP relationship.
risks: Catastrophe losses from storms and wildfires are rising
Commercial insurance pricing has softened after several strong years
Reserve adequacy on older liability policies is an industry-wide concern
opportunities: Revenue grew about 7% last year with a 14% net margin
Small business insurance is its most profitable line and has been growing
Higher interest rates raise the income earned on its investment portfolio
watch: The combined ratio in Business Insurance and premium growth.
